title: Boards, packaging and wiring
blurb: What holds a circuit together: the board itself, the packages, the solder, the cable and the box it lives in.

items.s: A printed circuit board (PCB), also known as a printed wiring board (PWB), is a laminated sandwich structure of conductive and insulating layers, each with a pattern of traces, planes and other features (similar to wires on a flat surfac…
A breadboard, solderless breadboard, or protoboard is a construction base used to build semi-permanent prototypes of electronic circuits.
Perfboard is a material for prototyping electronic circuits.

Stripboard is the generic name for a widely used type of electronics prototyping material for circuit boards characterized by a pre-formed 0.1 inches (2.54 mm) regular (rectangular) grid of holes, with wide parallel strips of copper clad…

Flexible electronics, also known as flex circuits, encompass various technologies that are used for assembling electronic circuits by mounting electronic components on flexible plastic substrates, such as polyimide, PEEK, or transparent…
Printed electronics is a set of printing methods used to create electrical devices on various substrates.

In electronics, through-hole technology (also spelled "thru-hole") is a manufacturing scheme in which leads on the components are inserted through holes drilled in printed circuit boards (PCB) and soldered to pads on the opposite side, e…
Surface-mount technology (SMT), originally called planar mounting, is a method in which the electrical components are mounted directly onto the surface of a printed circuit board (PCB).
A ball grid array (BGA) is a type of surface-mount packaging (a chip carrier) used for integrated circuits.
In microelectronics, a dual in-line package (DIP or DIL) is an electronic component package with a rectangular housing and two parallel rows of electrical connecting pins.

A small outline integrated circuit (SOIC) is a surface-mounted integrated circuit (IC) package which occupies an area about 30–50% less than an equivalent dual in-line package (DIP), with a typical thickness being 70% less.
A quad flat package (QFP) is a surface-mounted integrated circuit package with "gull wing" leads extending from each of the four sides.
A pin header (or simply, header) is a form of electrical connector.
In electronics, a chip carrier is one of several kinds of surface-mount technology packages for integrated circuits (commonly called "chips").
Solder (UK: ; NA: ) is a fusible metal alloy used to create a permanent bond between metal workpieces.
Solder paste is a preparation of powdered solder in sticky flux paste primarily used to solder surface mount components onto printed circuit boards.
Soldering (US: ; UK: ) joins two metal surfaces using a filler metal called solder.
In electronics, desoldering is the removal of soldered components from a circuit board for troubleshooting, repair, replacement, and salvage.
Wire wrap is an electronic component assembly technique that was invented to wire telephone crossbar switches, and later adapted to construct electronic circuit boards.
A wire is a flexible, round bar of metal.
An electrical cable is an assembly of one or more wires running side by side or bundled, which is used as an electrical conductor to carry electric current.
A ribbon cable is a cable with many conducting wires running parallel to each other on the same flat plane.

Coaxial cable, or coax (pronounced ), is a type of electrical cable consisting of an inner center conductor surrounded by a concentric conducting shield, with the two separated by a dielectric (insulating material); many coaxial cables a…
Twisted pair cabling is a type of communications cable in which two conductors of a single circuit are twisted together for the purposes of improving electromagnetic compatibility.

An electrical enclosure, power box (US), or feeder pillar (UK), is a cabinet for electrical or electronic equipment to mount switches, knobs and displays and to prevent electrical shock to equipment users and protect the contents from th…
A DIN rail is a metal rail of a standard type widely used for mounting circuit breakers and industrial control equipment inside equipment racks.
A 19-inch rack is a standardized frame or enclosure for mounting multiple electronic equipment modules.
A screw is an externally helical threaded fastener capable of being tightened or released by a twisting force (torque) to the head.
A cable tie (also known as a hose tie, panduit, tie wrap, wire tie, Steggel tie or zip tie) is a type of fastener for holding items together, primarily electrical cables and wires.
A grommet is a ring or edge strip inserted into a hole through thin material, typically a sheet of textile fabric, sheet metal or composite of carbon fiber, wood or honeycomb.
